result.report:
PASS for the exact partial theorem: finite separable transport of the ordinary zero-Hessian equation on good, separated, strict, boundaryless pure analytic curves, including singular and nonreduced curves, and for the fixed-support differentiated approximation (2). This does not close original P06.2.

The dependency chain is complete: affinoid and ordinary-form foundations → finite fibres and full-fibre shrinking → compact partitions and whole-fibre scalar descriptions → polynomial approximation and polarization → orbit coefficients and Newton hulls → tangential mollification → calibrated carrier total variation → every invariant compact scalar test → real Galois averaging and scalar projection → normal-closure descent. I checked the supplied supporting arguments directly; artifact names, receipts, diagnostics and claimed prior inspections supply no premises.

Section 3 establishes the finite tensor algebra without reduction or division by the group order. Tensoring the fixed-space kernel proves B^G=A in every characteristic. The fibre algebra is a product of finite fields, and the invariant-idempotent argument proves transitivity while allowing nontrivial stabilizers. Compact inverse images and full-fibre shrinking follow from finite affinoid neighbourhood covers and compact complements, rather than a covering-space assertion. The purity argument correctly identifies contractions of upstairs minimal primes and preserves their dimensions by finite integral extensions. Reduction is used only for this dimension argument; the actual algebras remain in the calibration calculations. Goodness, strictness, separatedness, boundarylessness and ordinary-open restrictions have the required hypotheses.

Section 4 constructs precisely the compact-F finite partition required by the task. Division by the positive finite sum and extension by zero are legitimate on the stated compact supports. The disjoint full-fibre pieces admit analytic idempotents and glued units in the actual affinoid algebra. Their selector logarithms produce one smooth scalar description on the whole upstairs affinoid. This establishes the hypothesis needed for the subsequent polynomial approximation without presuming smooth scalar descent.

The polynomial approximation in Section 5 controls derivatives through order two. Polarization spans every scalar monomial, including repeated variables and mixed correlations, by powers of logarithms of actual product units. All divisions here are real divisions. For each orbit polynomial, every group element contributes a root, including repetitions from stabilizers. The strict-gap coefficient argument proves the Newton rule despite characteristic-p cancellation. Both endpoint coefficients are retained; coefficients vanishing at the chosen point are uniformly above the endpoint chord after shrinking, and every other retained coefficient is made an actual downstairs unit. Thus no zero coefficient is logarithmed or silently discarded.

The new smoothing step is established. At a hull change, gradients telescope across collinear refinements, giving C¹ matching. The finitely many polynomial chamber Hessians are locally bounded; continuity of the gradient removes singular face terms from the weak Hessian. For a segment contained entirely in a collision face, every incident chamber has the same tangential second derivative at its interior points. Convolution consequently converges in that tangent direction. Finite subdivision also handles transverse crossings, deficient-rank height maps and constant height maps. This is stronger than C⁰ density and is sufficient specifically because curve tests are scalar.

Section 8 converts these tangential estimates into total variation on the actual carrier. On each supporting skeletal cell, the error and the positive reference form contract against the same canonical calibration. The finite calibrated subdivision, bounded Hessians and almost-everywhere tangential convergence give bounded convergence before any signed pushforward. Actual finite-flat degrees and Artinian lengths multiply both sides of the domination estimate; they are never replaced by fibre point counts. Lower-dimensional faces contribute no top measure. The product rule handles the scalar, first-derivative and second-derivative cutoff errors.

Section 9 correctly orders the two approximation limits. The coefficient C² error is estimated using fixed outer cutoffs and fixed upstairs tuples. Each individual polynomial is then localized using finitely many traces, neighbourhoods and inner cutoffs chosen before its smoothing limit. These choices may vary with polynomial degree, but smoothing is chosen afterward and every approximant remains inside the same outer compact C. Hence (2) holds for every invariant compact ordinary scalar test, and boundedness of each continuous finite multiplier on π⁻¹(C) proves (25).

The normalization factors in Section 10 are correct. Scalar projection preserves canonical top measures without [E:K]. Restricting the same carrier from E to K introduces [E:K]; an actual K-analytic Galois automorphism has calibrated degree one, so cancelling that common factor proves upstairs invariance. Real averaging then retains the pairing of every compact test. Equation (26) proves actual reverse descent, and applying it to N/E after Galois ascent over N/K proves ascent for every finite separable E/K. The cubic construction independently proves a complete degree-three field with residue F₈ and value group Z, then uses the supplied Newton iteration to split the separable cubic. Its Galois group is cyclic of order three.

Harmless wording corrections: write (t_gf)^k in (10), removing the stray comma, and make the implicit non-Archimedean ground-field convention explicit. CLD 12.2.4's printed dimension-equality wording must not be certified: constant moments disprove it. The draft already avoids that wording, using only polyhedrality and the separate upper bound in 12.2.10; the cited underlying [Ducros Theorem 3.2](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.1142/S1793744212500077.pdf#page=40) confirms the needed statement. No substantial repair or additional hypothesis is required. Higher-dimensional alternating tests, infinite extensions, classical recognition and positive-current regularization remain outside the proved scope.

passages.statement: For a complete non-Archimedean field K and a K-affinoid algebra A, M(A) is compact Hausdorff, A is noetherian with closed ideals, and the kernel map M(A)→Spec(A) is surjective. Every point of M(A) has rational affinoid neighbourhoods inside any prescribed ordinary open neighbourhood. Good analytic spaces have affinoid neighbourhood bases; ordinary opens are analytic domains; analytic sections form a sheaf for ordinary opens; and O(M(A))=A. These are the affinoid statements of CLD 11.1.1–2 and 11.1.5–8.

Affinoid fibre products and complete scalar extensions are formed using completed tensor products, and scalar projection is surjective (CLD 11.1.9). A finite algebra over a K-affinoid algebra, equipped with its finite-module Banach topology, is K-affinoid (CLD 11.4.4). Over a nontrivially valued complete non-Archimedean field, every point of a good strict analytic space has a strict affinoid neighbourhood (CLD 11.7.7).

Separated analytic spaces are Hausdorff. Strict affinoid analytic dimension equals Krull dimension; analytic dimension is preserved by complete scalar extension. If X_i are the minimal-prime components of an affinoid X, then dim_x(X)=sup_{x∈X_i} dim(X_i). For every analytic domain V⊂X and every x∈V, dim_x(V)=dim_x(X). These are CLD 11.2.2–3.

For morphisms of non-Archimedean analytic spaces, the relative interior of an analytic domain inclusion is its ordinary topological interior, and Int(Y/Z)∩f⁻¹(Int(Z/S))⊂Int(Y/S). For every analytic extension L/K, ∂(Y_L/Z_L)⊂π⁻¹(∂(Y/Z)). These are GR 2.11(3)–(5); in particular ordinary opens and scalar extensions of boundaryless spaces are boundaryless.

On a topologically separated non-Archimedean analytic space, ordinary CLD forms admit local unit-moment descriptions on ordinary open neighbourhoods in every bidegree. Ordinary smooth scalar functions admit descriptions φ(−log|f_1|,…,−log|f_m|) with analytic units f_i and smooth Euclidean φ. Ordinary forms form an ordinary sheaf stable under wedge, J, d′ and d″; moment pullback commutes with these operations. For a G-tropical chart f and a coefficient form a, f* a is zero in the G-form sheaf exactly when a restricts to zero on f(V) for every compact domain V. These are CLD 15.1.1(b), 15.1.2, 6.2.1–2, 3.3.12 and 3.4.4.

A good Hausdorff analytic space is locally holomorphically separated. On a locally holomorphically separated analytic space, for every compact F and ordinary open neighbourhood U of F, there is an ordinary smooth function equal to one near F with compact support contained in U. This is CLD 15.2.2 and Corollary 15.2.5, with its compact-cutoff proof through 6.2.4 and A.2.4.

Let K be a complete non-Archimedean field and Γ⊂R_{>0} a subgroup with Γ·|K×| nontrivial. If Y is compact and Γ-strict of dimension d and f_1,…,f_m are analytic units on Y, then the image under their absolute values is a finite c-polytope of dimension at most d, where c=(Q,(|K×|·Γ)^Q). Equivalently its logarithmic image is a finite polyhedral set of dimension at most d. This is Ducros, Espaces de Berkovich, polytopes, squelettes et théorie des modèles, Theorem 3.2(1), underlying the polyhedrality assertion cited in CLD 12.2.4. CLD 12.2.10 separately gives dim_trop,x(f)≤d_K(x)≤dim_x(Y) and, for compact Y, dim(f_trop(Y))=sup_x dim_trop,x(f).

passages.statement: A pure n-dimensional Hausdorff analytic space, with its canonical calibration and analytic boundary, is a tropical space of level n; the induced tropical structure on an analytic domain agrees with that domain's analytic structure (CLD 15.7.1–2). Every compact tropical chart is pleasant and its tropical polyhedron is the n-dimensional part of its moment image (CLD 5.4.4). For a compact analytic moment domain, its supporting characteristic skeleton admits a finite compatible subdivision into convenient cells on which the tropicalization is injective (CLD 14.1.11–12).

Canonical calibrations are standard and positive. On a top moment cell Q, its calibration is d_Q τ_{Q,*}|e_1∧⋯∧e_n|, where τ_Q is the affine inverse of an injective torus projection and d_Q is the sum of the actual finite-flat degrees of the skeletal cells above Q, including the dimensions of nonreduced Artinian fibre algebras (CLD 14.3.2–5 and 14.5.1–2). A top form's carrier measure is obtained by contraction on its supporting skeleton (CLD 5.8.3–5). For a pleasant chart f and a Borel (n,n) coefficient form a, its induced measure is locally finite exactly when a is locally integrable on the calibrated tropical polyhedron, and then f_*((f* a)_Rad)=⟨a,μ_{Π_f}⟩_Rad and the corresponding integrals agree (CLD 5.10.1(c,d)). Smooth top forms have finite total variation on compact moment domains; lower-dimensional cells have no top measure.

For a level-n analytic space and any complete scalar extension L/K, scalar projection sends the canonical calibration of the extended skeleton to the original calibration (CLD 14.3.6). For a tropically Borel (n,n) G-form ω, π_*ω_{L,Bor}=ω_Bor; when ω is locally integrable, π_*ω_{L,Rad}=ω_Rad, without a field-degree factor (CLD 15.3.1). The underlying degree identity states that, for a morphism f:Y→Z, a point y over z and any chosen target lift z_L, deg_y(f) equals the sum of deg_w(f_L) over lifts w of y above z_L (CLD 13.3.3(a)); zero-dimensional degrees use actual Artinian fibre-algebra dimensions.

For a finite extension F/K and an F-analytic space Z of level n, restriction to its K-analytic structure on the same carrier preserves dimensions and skeletal subsets and multiplies canonical calibration by [F:K] (CLD 14.4.3). For level-n analytic spaces and a morphism f finite above the complement of a Zariski closed set of dimension less than n, a locally integrable (p,n) G-form ω, with p∈{n−1,n}, has locally integrable pullback and f_*((f*ω)_Rad)=dc(f)ω_Rad (CLD 15.4.1–3). An analytic isomorphism has calibrated degree one.

On a tropical space of level n, a locally integrable multiplier u defines the integration current [u] by pairing compact ordinary top tests with their Radon measures; continuous finite multipliers are locally integrable (CLD 7.3.5 and 5.7.2). Current duality satisfies ⟨d′d″S,α⟩=⟨S,d′d″α⟩ for compact ordinary tests of the appropriate bidegree (CLD 7.7.5).
